headline: Toy donkey goes home after a week on a ferry

sources.title: Watch: Stuffed donkey returned to 5-year-old after social media adventure
Happy ending for honorary BC Ferries crew member Churro as owner found
Churro the Burro's adventure on BC Ferries delights thousands
How a BC Ferries crew found the owner of 'Churro' the stuffed donkey (video, CTV News)

chunks.text: A pink [[stuffed]] donkey {{turned up}} on the BC Ferries [[vessel]] Salish Raven on Thursday, July 16. The company believes it was {{left behind}} on an afternoon [[sailing]] from Swartz Bay to the Southern Gulf Islands, British Columbia. No one had {{come forward}} to claim it. The [[crew]] named it Churro the Burro, gave it a staff [[badge]], and began posting photographs of its days [[at sea]]. [[By the time]] the owner was found, the toy had spent a week [[aboard]].

verbs.correct: To appear or be found, often unexpectedly
verbs.wrong: To refuse to accept an offer or request
verbs.why: A missing sock can turn up months later in the laundry, and an old friend might turn up at a reunion unannounced. A pink stuffed donkey turned up on the ferry Salish Raven on July 16.

verbs.correct: To forget something and go without it
verbs.wrong: To not include something in a list
verbs.why: A tired traveler can leave behind an umbrella on a train, and a rushed guest might leave behind a jacket at a party. The ferry company believes a young passenger left behind the toy donkey on an afternoon sailing.

verbs.correct: To make yourself known to claim something
verbs.wrong: To be mentioned or talked about online
verbs.why: A witness comes forward with new details after a crash, and an owner comes forward to claim a lost wallet. For days, no one came forward to claim the little stuffed donkey found on the ship.

chunks.text: BC Ferries carries passengers between Vancouver Island, the mainland and the smaller islands. Instead of a [[plain]] [[lost-and-found]] notice, the company asked the public online to help {{track down}} the owner, and the crew {{showed Churro around}} the ship. There are photographs of it on the bridge, in the engine room, on [[deck]], and in the gift shop among the other stuffed animals. Others show it with a book and a soft serve ice cream.

verbs.correct: To search for someone until you find them
verbs.wrong: To follow how something changes over time
verbs.why: A detective tracks down a missing suspect, and an old classmate can track down a friend she has not seen in years. The ferry company asked the public online to help track down the donkey's owner.

verbs.correct: To take someone on a tour of a place
verbs.wrong: To let a visitor in at the entrance
verbs.why: A tour guide shows visitors around an old castle, and a new coworker gets shown around the office on the first day. The crew showed Churro around the ferry, from the bridge to the engine room.

chunks.text: The [[posts]] {{racked up}} more than a million views and thousands of comments. Some people [[suggested]] Churro {{stay on}} as a [[mascot]]. On Monday, July 20, the company said the search was over. The donkey [[belonged to]] five-year-old Alfie, whose grandmother had bought it for him in Mexico. His mother, Abigail Broadribb, had not noticed it was [[missing]] [[at all]]. She {{came across}} the story [[in the news]].

verbs.correct: To collect a large number or amount of something
verbs.wrong: To make sense when you look at all the facts
verbs.why: A popular video can rack up millions of views overnight, and a busy shop racks up long lines on a Saturday. The photos of Churro racked up more than a million views and thousands of comments.

verbs.correct: To remain in a place or role longer than expected
verbs.wrong: To agree to join a company as a new worker
verbs.why: A helpful employee can stay on past closing time, and a popular teacher might stay on for one more year. Some fans suggested that Churro stay on as the ferry's official mascot.

verbs.wrong: To seem or appear a certain way
verbs.why: You can come across an old photo while cleaning a closet, and a reader might come across a great recipe in a magazine. Alfie's mother came across the story completely by chance while reading the news.

chunks.text: The company thanked everyone who had commented, tagged friends and shared the posts, then [[arranged]] a [[reunion]] for later that week. Churro was {{handed back}} to Alfie, keeping the name the crew gave it. "We're just really [[grateful]]," Broadribb said. "This is a very special experience for him to have [[a peek behind the curtain]]."

verbs.correct: To return something to the person it belongs to
verbs.wrong: To give something to a younger family member
verbs.why: A teacher hands back graded essays the next week, and a librarian hands back a returned book to its shelf. After a week at sea, Churro was finally handed back to five-year-old Alfie.

mainIdea.s: A stuffed donkey left on a Canadian ferry became a social media star while crew searched for its owner. By the time the owner was found, the toy had spent a week aboard the ship.
mainIdea.why: The crew posted photos of the toy while looking for its owner. By the time the owner was found, the toy had spent a week aboard.

mainIdea.s: The boy's worried mother spent a week searching online after she noticed her son's donkey was missing. The ferry company then asked the public for help finding the donkey's owner.
mainIdea.why: Close, but Alfie's mother had not noticed the toy was missing at all. She only found out because she saw the story in the news, not because she went searching.

mainIdea.s: BC Ferries canceled several sailings between Vancouver Island and the mainland last month due to a mechanical fault. The company said service fully returned to normal within two days.
mainIdea.why: This story is about a mechanical fault that canceled ferry sailings, not the stuffed donkey found on board.
